1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nxe4.name: Petrov's Defence: Damiano Variation
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nxe4.background: Introduced by Pedro Damiano in his Libro da Imparare a Giocare a Scacchi, one of the oldest books on "modern rules" chess. It is usually regarded as an error, though it has occasionally been seen in recent grandmaster play.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nxe4 4.Qe2.strategy: Attacks the knight and lines the queen up on the open e-file behind it. If the knight runs, White's knight can move with a discovered check, which is why ...Nf6?? loses at once to Nc6+, winning the queen. Black has to find the best defence.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nxe4 4.Qe2 Qe7.strategy: Black's best reply: the queen steps onto the e-file, so that after White takes the knight on e4 the white knight on e5 is pinned to its queen and can be hit with ...d6. Black ends a pawn down for open lines and quick development; White keeps a modest edge.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nxe4 4.Qe2 Qe7.name: Petrov's Defence: Damiano Variation, Kholmov Gambit
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nxe4 4.Qe2 Qe7.background: Pedro Damiano gave 4.Qe2 Qe7 in his Libro da Imparare a Giocare a Scacchi, one of the oldest books on chess under the modern rules; the line now bears the name of the Kholmov Gambit.
